description: A fully open-source humanoid arm for physical AI research and deployment in contact-rich environments.

summary.one_liner: OpenArm is an open-source 7-DOF humanoid arm and surrounding software ecosystem for physical AI research, teleoperation, and data collection in contact-rich environments.
summary.what_it_does: The README presents OpenArm as a human-scale 7-DOF arm with high backdrivability and compliance, aimed at safe human-robot interaction and practical payloads. It describes a standardized "OpenArm Cell" environment with fixed background, lighting, and camera placement so research can be reproduced under consistent conditions. The project is organized as a set of linked repositories: hardware CAD/BOM, URDF description, a CAN motor control library, ros2_control and MoveIt packages, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab models and RL tasks, a dataset format with Python API and LeRobot conversion, and leader-follower teleoperation. A motorless leader arm called OpenArm KER (with firmware) and dora-rs based dataflows for teleoperation, data collection, and policy inference are also covered. The README states a complete bimanual system costs $6,500 USD and can be bought assembled or as a DIY build.
use_cases: physical AI research on contact-rich manipulation
simulating an arm in MuJoCo or Isaac Lab
policy inference and evaluation on real hardware
building a bimanual robot from open hardware designs
how_to_run: Browse the Core and dora-rs tables in the README and choose the repository for your task (e.g., openarm_ros2, openarm_mujoco, dora-openarm-data-collection)
Follow the per-repository Docs or Tutorial links at docs.openarm.dev
Clone the chosen repository and follow its own install instructions (not included in this README)
notable: Open hardware: CAD, STL and BOM released under CERN-OHL-S-2.0 in openarm_hardware
Standardized OpenArm Cell for reproducible evaluation conditions
Motorless KER leader arm with the same kinematics as OpenArm 2.0
Multiple simulation and robotics stacks: MuJoCo, Isaac Lab, ROS 2 and MoveIt, dora-rs
caveats: Arm support varies by version: several repositories are only partly supported for 2.0 (marked as adaptation needed or work in progress), and Isaac Lab is work in progress for 2.0
The README says the project is in continuous development
Complete bimanual system priced at $6,500 USD; purchase is part of the project's commercial side
